stages.title: PART IVA: ORIGIN AND AMENDMENT HISTORY

groups.heading: ORIGINAL DESIGN
items: No separate citizen-duty list existed in 1950.
State duties appeared in Part IV.
USSR is the conventional source influence.

groups.heading: 1976 INSERTION
items: Swaran Singh Committee recommended eight duties.
The 42nd Amendment inserted Part IVA and ten duties.
Rejected proposals are not constitutional text.

groups.heading: 2002 ADDITION
items: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 51A(k).
It concerns education opportunity for a child or ward aged six to fourteen.
Total today: eleven duties.

stages.answer_line: The duty is framed as providing opportunities for education to a child or ward aged six to fourteen; the constitutional clause itself does not prescribe a criminal punishment.

stages.title: ALL ELEVEN DUTIES: EXACT GROUPED RECALL

groups.heading: CONSTITUTION AND NATION
items: (a) Constitution, institutions, Flag and Anthem.
(b) freedom-struggle ideals.
(c) sovereignty, unity and integrity.
(d) defence and national service when called.

groups.heading: SOCIETY, CULTURE AND REASON
items: (e) harmony, brotherhood and dignity of women.
(f) composite heritage.
(g) environment and compassion.
(h) scientific temper, humanism, inquiry and reform.

groups.heading: PUBLIC ETHIC AND CAPABILITY
items: (i) public property and non-violence.
(j) individual and collective excellence.
(k) education opportunity, ages six to fourteen.

stages.answer_line: Article 51A(k) places the educational duty on a citizen who is a parent or guardian, not on the State or every citizen indiscriminately.

stages.title: LEGAL CHARACTER: NON-JUSTICIABLE BUT RELEVANT

groups.heading: TEXTUAL STATUS
items: Article 51A addresses every citizen.
The duties are non-justiciable.
Article 51A alone creates neither writ nor penalty.

groups.heading: LEGAL MEDIATION
items: Legislatures enact valid laws within competence.
The executive implements law and civic education.
Courts may use duty values in interpretation.

groups.heading: CONSTITUTIONAL LIMIT
items: Implementing laws remain subject to rights.
No separate statute exists for every duty.
A broad duty cannot validate disproportionate moral policing.

stages.answer_line: The Constitution does not label clauses as "moral" or "civic." The classification is analytical, clauses overlap, and no legal conclusion automatically follows from the label.
source_references: notes\Final-Learning-Packages\_deep-content-review\reviews\polity-09\g3-source\polity-09_g3-reviewed-source.md#03. Legal character: what Article 51A can and cannot do

stages.title: RIGHTS, DUTIES AND DPSP: CORRELATIVE CONSTITUTIONALISM

groups.heading: THREE DIRECTIONS
items: Part III protects enforceable claims.
Part IV directs State welfare purpose.
Part IVA states citizen responsibilities.

groups.heading: RELATIONSHIP
items: Rights protect responsible agency.
Duties sustain civic conditions for liberty.
DPSP guides institutions toward justice.

groups.heading: LIMITS
items: Duty cannot erase a right.
Right does not immunise violence or illegality.
Harmony cannot replace exact text.

stages.answer_line: Bijoe Emmanuel (1986) is the clearest control: respectful standing without singing the Anthem was protected by Articles 19(1)(a) and 25(1).

stages.title: NATIONAL SYMBOLS: RESPECT WITHOUT COMPULSION

groups.heading: CONSCIENCE
items: Bijoe Emmanuel (1986) protected respectful non-singing.
Freedom of conscience defeated compelled vocal conformity.
Respect and participation differ.

groups.heading: FLAG EXPRESSION
items: Naveen Jindal (2004) treated respectful Flag display as expression.
Restrictions require valid law within Article 19.
Executive instructions cannot independently create every restriction.

groups.heading: ANTHEM CONTROL
items: The 2016 cinema direction was interim.
The 9 January 2018 final order made cinema playing optional or directory.
Do not state the superseded mandate as current law.

stages.answer_line: Constitutional patriotism protects the symbols of the Republic while refusing to reduce civic loyalty to a single compelled performance.

stages.title: HARMONY, CULTURE, REASON AND ECOLOGY

groups.heading: SOCIAL CITIZENSHIP
items: 51A(e): harmony, brotherhood and dignity of women.
51A(f): composite cultural heritage.
Neither clause licenses cultural uniformity.

groups.heading: RATIONAL CITIZENSHIP
items: 51A(h): scientific temper, humanism, inquiry and reform.
Inquiry joins evidence with openness to correction.
It is not State-defined orthodoxy.

groups.heading: ECOLOGICAL CITIZENSHIP
items: 51A(g): environment and compassion.
It works with Article 48A, Article 21 and statutes.
The 2023 Jallikattu ruling qualifies the 2014 reading.

stages.answer_line: Harmony laws must be applied to the exact offence, not to suppress unpopular but lawful argument.

stages.title: PUBLIC PROPERTY, EXCELLENCE AND EDUCATION

groups.heading: PUBLIC ETHIC
items: 51A(i) protects public property and rejects violence.
Peaceful protest remains protected.
Property damage is governed by valid law.

groups.heading: EXCELLENCE
items: 51A(j) concerns individual and collective excellence.
It is aspirational.
It creates no automatic admission entitlement.

groups.heading: EDUCATION TRIAD
items: Article 21A: State right, ages six to fourteen.
Article 45: early childhood below six.
51A(k): parent or guardian duty, ages six to fourteen.

stages.answer_line: "Abjure violence" is broader than property damage, but it does not erase the right to assemble peacefully or protest.

stages.title: VERMA COMMITTEE, EXISTING LAW AND REFORM

groups.heading: COMMITTEE APPROACH
items: The Verma Committee stressed education and awareness.
It mapped existing laws that effectuate duties.
It did not require a separate statute for every clause.

groups.heading: IMPLEMENTATION WEB
items: National Honour, civil-rights, security and election laws cover several duties.
Environmental laws support 51A(g).
Public-property and education laws support 51A(i) and (k).

groups.heading: REFORM TEST
items: Identify the concrete legal gap.
Prefer education or civil measures when adequate.
Penal law must be narrow and rights-compliant.

stages.answer_line: Laws may operationalise Fundamental Duties, but their validity and purpose cannot be attributed solely to Article 51A.

stages.title: PRELIMS TRAPS AND VERIFIED PYQ ROUTES

groups.heading: PRELIMS CONTROL
items: 42nd inserted ten; 86th inserted clause (k).
Duties are citizen-only and non-justiciable.
51A(g) differs from 48A; 51A(k) differs from 21A and 45.

groups.heading: PYQ STATUS
items: No direct routed PYQ appears in maintained 2018-2025 ledgers.
2020 Q8 and 2025 Q55 support this topic but remain owned by Polity 08.
2025 key is official locally; 2020 remains inferred.

groups.heading: ANTI-FABRICATION
items: Keep exact wording and ownership.
Do not relabel coaching practice as UPSC PYQ.
State key confidence and source.

stages.answer_line: A missing direct PYQ is not a licence to invent one; supporting questions retain their original ownership.

Prove statutory ingredients and procedure.

Two named effects or examples.
One limit and direct verdict.

groups.heading: 15 MARKS
items: Mechanism through law, interpretation and education.
Counterargument and institutional reform.
Qualified answer to the directive.

stages.answer_line: Fundamental Duties are a grammar of responsible freedom whose legal force must remain precise, mediated and rights-compatible.
